items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: Alphonso Trent's band used to come through there, and he had a great band.

ctx.x: the piano. So he said with the bugle horn, you transpose a third down, a minor third down. And when he showed that to me, that was an easy transposition, because if a note is on the second line on the piano, your note will be on the first line for you. The only thing that you have to change is the signature. It don't (?). And it's funny about how that makes a note, even when you... If you've got an A-flat, your note will be F-natural. And if you've got an A-natural, your note will be F-sharp; you've got to make…

And I had... See, I didn't have no idea I had this talent for music. But in Oklahoma, in them early days, we heard so many good bands nad good Blues players, and guys played piano. Alphonso Trent's band used to come through there, and he had a great band. And I heard this, and that music was kind of in my ear. But I didn't discern(?) it until I started to fool around with it.
